doc.summary: Where each boundary's faces lie.

returns.desc: ``{name: {'n_faces', 'interior_faces', 'status'}}`` with ``status`` one of ``'empty'`` (no faces), ``'boundary'`` (all on the skin of the domain), ``'interior'`` (all with a cell on each side: an inner zone) or ``'mixed'``.

doc.summary: Compare the zones of the mesh with the BCs declared in files.
doc.description:
Names are compared without case: HOPR writes them in lower case
(``sidea``) while ANSA and the files keep ``sideA``.

Rules, from what HORSES3D and PyHOPE actually do:

* HORSES3D needs a ``#define boundary`` with a ``type`` for every
  zone that has faces, **inner zones included** (their type is never
  applied, but the solver stops without it). A zone with no faces
  needs nothing.
* PyHOPE needs a ``BoundaryName`` for every surface group of a
  ``.cgns``/``.msh``, and an inner zone must have type 100: any other
  type stops it with "internal face with multiple BCs". Type 100 on
  a zone that lies on the skin of the domain is a mistake too.
* A name declared in a file but absent from the mesh is reported as
  a warning: harmless for the solver, but usually a sign that the
  file belongs to another mesh.

params.name: control
params.desc: HORSES3D ``.control`` file.

params.name: ini
params.desc: PyHOPE ``parameter.ini``.

returns.desc: ``rows``: one per name (union of mesh and files), with ``name``, ``mesh`` (status, None if absent), ``n_faces``, ``control`` (type, None if absent), ``ini`` (type tuple); and ``issues``.

doc.summary: Check the skin of the domain.
doc.description:
The exterior faces of a sound volume mesh form closed surfaces: every
edge of the skin belongs to exactly two exterior faces. An edge with
one face is a hole (typically a non-conforming interface or two zones
whose nodes were not merged); with three or more, surfaces touch
along a line.

returns.desc: ``exterior_faces``, ``unassigned_faces`` (in no boundary), ``nonmanifold_faces`` (more than two cells), ``open_edges``, ``nonmanifold_edges``, ``faces_in_two_boundaries``, ``mixed_boundaries`` (names of BCs partly inner, partly on the skin), ``closed`` (no open edges) and ``issues``.

doc.summary: Find nodes that coincide in space but are different nodes.
doc.description:
Three things come out of the same search, and they mean different
things:

* duplicates among **high-order nodes only** (edge or face nodes
  written once per element): harmless for the topology, which only
  looks at corners; PyHOPE merges them when it writes the ``.h5``;
* coincident **exterior faces** (cracks): two faces in the same
  place that the topology sees as different, so the domain is cut
  along them and both count as skin;
* **collapsed cells**: two nodes of one cell in the same place.

params.name: rtol
params.desc: Tolerance relative to the bounding-box diagonal.

returns.desc: ``tol``, ``groups`` (sets of coincident nodes), ``extra_nodes`` (nodes that merging would remove), ``corner_groups`` (groups with two or more corner nodes), ``highorder_groups``, ``crack_faces``, ``collapsed_cells`` and ``issues``.

doc.summary: Compare this mesh with another one, cell by cell and BC by BC.
doc.description:
Meant for the same mesh in two formats (``.cgns`` and its ``.h5``)
or at two geometric orders (g2 and g4 of one ANSA mesh): cells are
paired by the centroid of their corners, so the comparison does not
depend on how the files number them, and the corners must coincide.
Areas of curved boundaries differ a little between orders; that is
expected and reported, not flagged.

params.name: other
params.desc: The mesh to compare with.

params.name: rtol
params.desc: Tolerance relative to this mesh's bounding-box diagonal.

returns.desc: ``cells`` (both counts), ``matched_cells``, ``max_corner_diff``, ``same_corners``, ``boundaries`` (rows ``name``, ``faces``, ``area`` as pairs and ``area_rel_diff``), ``only_here``, ``only_there``, ``orders`` and ``issues``.

doc.summary: Would HORSES3D's actuator disk find these points?
doc.description:
Replicates ``FindActuatorPointElementAD``: the elements are split
among ``nranks`` ranks in contiguous blocks of the file's element
order; a point is found when some rank's *first* element (lowest
index) whose trilinear shape holds it also holds it with the curved
shape. With ``inner_curves=False`` (``mesh inner curves = .false.``)
only elements with a boundary face are curved.

params.name: points

params.desc: MPI ranks of the run.

params.name: inner_curves
params.desc: The solver's ``mesh inner curves``. Default True (its default).

params.name: tol
params.desc: Tolerance on the reference coordinates.

returns.desc: ``found`` (bool per point), ``cell`` (the element that would take it, -1 if none), ``honest`` (:meth:`points`'s answer, to compare), ``lost`` (indices of points inside the fluid that HORSES3D would not find) and ``max_xi`` (largest curved ``|xi|`` among the elements whose trilinear shape holds each point: values just above 1 flag points at risk for other numbers of ranks).

doc.summary: Warn when high-order hexahedra fail the tensor-order screen.
Node orderings: the canonical layout of LEGOLAS and how each format maps to it.

text_sections.title: Canonical layout
text_sections.text:
* **Hexahedra and quadrilaterals of any order** are stored in *tensor* order,
  ``i`` fastest: node ``(i, j, k)`` of an order-``N`` hexahedron is at
  position ``i + (N+1) j + (N+1)**2 k``. This is the layout of HOPR/PyHOPE
  ``*_mesh.h5`` files and of HORSES3D, and it makes interpolation and
  Jacobians a matter of tensor products. It applies to linear hexahedra too,
  so the 8 corners are **not** in VTK order (use :func:`hex_corners`).
* **Tetrahedra, pyramids and prisms** are linear only and keep the VTK/CGNS
  corner order (they coincide for these elements).

Local faces of a hexahedron follow the CGNS face order, which is also the
local side order of HOPR (``SideInfo``)::

    0: zeta = 0 (k = 0)   1: eta = 0 (j = 0)   2: xi = 1 (i = N)
    3: eta = 1 (j = N)    4: xi = 0 (i = 0)    5: zeta = 1 (k = N)

text_sections.title: Permutation tables
text_sections.text:
Each table ``perm`` maps a native element to the canonical one:
``canonical = native[perm]``. They were measured, not transcribed: gmsh
4.13.1 meshed a unit cube with a single element of order 1-4 and wrote it as
``.msh`` (v2.2 and v4.1) and ``.cgns``; rounding each node's coordinates to
the ``1/N`` grid gives its tensor index. The same reference files live in
``FotR/tests/data/legolas/`` and the tests repeat the measurement.

Two traps the tables encode:

* meshio reorders ``hexahedron27`` to the VTK layout but leaves
  ``hexahedron64`` and ``hexahedron125`` in gmsh's native order, so the
  meshio tables differ from the gmsh ones at order 2 only.
* CGNS and gmsh agree on corners and on the order-1 element, and differ
  from order 2 on (edges, faces and interior are numbered differently).

doc.summary: Check that hexahedra really are in tensor order.
doc.description:
Along every grid line of a correctly ordered element, consecutive nodes
advance in the direction of that line (``x[i+1] - x[i]`` has a positive
projection on ``x[N] - x[0]``), however curved the element is. A wrong
permutation sends some node backwards. It is a cheap screen, not a proof:
a permutation that happens to keep every line monotone would pass.

The corners must be right (they are whenever faces and boundaries match,
which is what the topology checks); each other node is placed in the
reference cube by inverting the trilinear map of the corners and rounded
to the ``1/N`` grid. Over a sample of cells, the most common position of
every node wins. Mildly curved cells give the same answer; the vote
absorbs the rest.

doc.summary: Geometry for the viewer: what gets drawn, as plain numpy arrays.
doc.description:
Everything here is independent of HTTP and of the browser, so it is tested
without either. The server (:mod:`.viewer`) only packs these arrays.

Surfaces are lists of element faces (see :class:`.mesh.Boundary`). A
high-order face is drawn through its own node grid, ``N x N`` quadrilaterals
split into two triangles each, so curvature shows at the nodes without any
interpolation. Next to the triangles go the **element edges** (the four
sides of every face, following the nodes), which is what shows the
connectivity; the diagonals of the triangulation are never drawn.

Positions are sent relative to :func:`origin` (the centre of the bounding
box) and in float32, which keeps sub-millimetre detail on domains of
kilometres.

doc.description:

is read: which zone names each file declares and with which type. Comments
start with ``!`` in both formats and are dropped; key names are matched
without case.

* ``.control``: blocks ``#define boundary a__b__c`` … ``type = X`` …
  ``#end``. Several zones share a block by joining their names with
  ``__`` (that is how HORSES3D splits them).
* ``parameter.ini``: pairs ``BoundaryName = x`` / ``BoundaryType =
  (/t,c,s,a/)``; the first integer of the type is the kind, and 100 marks
  an inner zone (faces with a cell on each side).

The GANDALF ring ``horses3d`` writes these blocks on its own; the two do not
share code on purpose (``doc/PLAN_HORSES3D.md``), so a change of syntax has
to be made in both.

doc.summary: ``LEGOLAS.Quality``: cell quality metrics, one value per cell.
doc.description:
Metrics (all per cell, in the global cell order of the mesh):

``scaled_jacobian``
    Minimum over the sample points of ``det J / (|x_xi| |x_eta| |x_zeta|)``
    (the Verdict measure): 1 for a perfect cube, 0 for a flat cell,
    negative for an inverted one. Higher is better.
``jacobian_ratio``
    ``min det J / max det J`` over the sample points: what PyHOPE prints as
    the "scaled Jacobian". 1 for an affine cell, <= 0 for an invalid one.
    Higher is better. Hexahedra only (NaN for the linear kinds, whose
    Jacobian is constant or piecewise constant).
``aspect_ratio``
    Longest over shortest corner edge. Lower is better; boundary layers are
    expected to be large.
``skewness``
    Equiangle skewness of the worst face, 0 (ideal angles) to 1
    (degenerate). Lower is better.
``non_orthogonality``
    Worst angle, in degrees, between a face normal and the line joining the
    centroids of the two cells it separates (inner faces only). Lower is
    better; it matters most to finite-volume solvers.
``volume_ratio``
    Largest ratio of volumes with a neighbour (>= 1). Lower is better.
``volume``
    Cell volume.

Where the Jacobian is evaluated: hexahedra of order N on the
``(N+1)**3`` Gauss-Lobatto points of the reference cube, from the Lagrange
interpolant through the geometric nodes, which every supported format places
at **equispaced** reference positions; for N = 1 those points are the
corners. Linear tetrahedra, prisms and pyramids use the three edges of each
corner (the apex of a pyramid has four and is skipped), normalised so that
the regular element scores 1.

Orientation: a format's convention may make every cell of a kind
"left-handed" (VTK and gmsh order the prism differently). Each block keeps
the orientation of its majority of cells; only the minority comes out
negative, and ``meta['flipped']`` says when a block was turned round.

Only numpy. SAM's finite-difference helpers are not used on purpose: they
would import SAM (and torch) into a module that must stay light.

doc.summary: Gauss-Lobatto points and weights on [-1, 1] for order *n* (n+1 points).
Lagrange basis through *nodes* and its derivative, evaluated at *x*.

returns.name: L, D
returns.desc: ``(len(x), len(nodes))``: ``L[a, i] = l_i(x_a)``, ``D[a, i] = l_i'(x_a)``.

doc.summary: For each corner, three neighbours ordered for a positive determinant on the reference element (corners with four neighbours are skipped).
Jacobian extremes at the Gauss-Lobatto points, per cell (chunked).

returns.desc: ``smin``, ``smax`` (scaled Jacobian), ``dmin``, ``dmax`` (det J) and ``vol`` (sum of det J times the GL weights), each ``(n_cells,)``.

doc.summary: Corner scaled Jacobians ``(n_cells, n_corners)``, normalised, and volume. The minimum is taken by the caller, once the block's orientation is known (taking it before turning the signs round would keep the best corner instead of the worst).
Interior angles (degrees) of polygons ``c`` (m, k, 3).
The *n* worst cells of any per-cell array.

params.name: values
params.desc: ``(n_cells,)``; NaN cells are skipped.

params.name: better
params.desc: ``'high'`` (lowest first), ``'low'`` or None (highest first).

params.name: n
params.desc: How many.

returns.desc: As :meth:`Quality.worst`.

doc.summary: ``LEGOLAS.Resolution``: is the mesh fine enough for an LES? (a priori)
doc.description:
Mesh design, not post-processing: sizes come from the geometry and wall
units from a skin-friction correlation, before any solution exists. The
real y+ of a run needs the wall shear of a ``.hsol`` and belongs to the
HORSES3D tools.

Per cell (:meth:`Resolution.sizes`):

``h``
    ``V**(1/3)``.
``h_min``, ``h_max``
    For hexahedra, the mean length of the four edges along each reference
    direction, measured along the high-order nodes; the smallest and the
    largest of the three. For the linear kinds, the shortest and longest
    corner edge.
``anisotropy``
    ``h_max / h_min``.
``delta``, ``delta_max``
    With the polynomial order ``p`` of the solution: ``h / (p + 1)`` and
    ``h_max / (p + 1)``, the usual effective resolution of a DG element
    with ``(p + 1)**3`` degrees of freedom.

At a wall (:meth:`Resolution.wall`), per wall face:

``y1``
    Thickness of the wall cell along the wall normal (extent of its corners
    measured from the plane of the wall face).
``y1_dof``
    With ``p``: height of the first solution node off the wall, the first
    inner Gauss-Lobatto point of order p (``0.5 y1`` for p = 2, ``0.276``
    for 3, ``0.173`` for 4). Meaningful for cells stacked on the wall.
``dt1``, ``dt2``
    Lengths of the wall face along its two directions (mean of opposite
    edges; for a triangle, the longest and shortest edge), divided by
    ``p + 1`` when ``p`` is given.
``growth``
    Thickness ratio between consecutive cells of the stack on that face,
    for ``layers - 1`` steps. The stack is followed through opposite faces
    (hexahedra and prisms), so it stops (NaN) at any other kind.

Wall units (:meth:`Resolution.yplus`): with ``U = 1``, ``nu = L / Re`` and
``u_tau = sqrt(Cf / 2)``, a length ``y`` is ``y Re sqrt(Cf / 2) / L`` in
wall units. ``Cf`` comes from a flat-plate correlation, turbulent
``0.026 Re_x**(-1/7)`` or laminar (Blasius) ``0.664 Re_x**(-1/2)``, with
``Re_x = Re x / L``: ``x`` is the distance from the leading edge along the
flow when a direction is given, or ``L`` otherwise. It is an estimate for
sizing the first cell, not a prediction of the flow.

doc.summary: Height of the first inner Gauss-Lobatto node of order *p*, as a fraction of the element thickness.
Arc length of polylines ``(m, n, 3)``.
Mean arc length of the four edges along i, j and k: ``(m, 3)``.
``LEGOLAS.Convert``: fix the node order, and write VTK and gmsh files.
doc.description:
* :meth:`Convert.detect_order` / :meth:`Convert.fix_order` -- find and undo
  a node permutation the reader could not know about (ANSA's order-4
  ``.msh``), voting with the geometry (:func:`.ordering.detect_hex_order`).
* :meth:`Convert.to_vtu` -- the volume as a VTK XML unstructured grid:
  Lagrange cells (VTK 72, ParaView shows them curved) or each element cut
  into ``N**3`` linear hexahedra; per-cell fields go as cell data, per-node
  fields as point data.
* :meth:`Convert.to_vtm` -- a multiblock with the volume and one block per
  boundary, which is how ParaView lists the BCs by name.
* :meth:`Convert.write_msh` -- gmsh 2.2 (binary), in gmsh's own node order,
  with the zones and boundaries as physical groups: what PyHOPE reads.

Writers use numpy only (VTK is not needed to write VTK files). Node orders
come from :mod:`.ordering`, measured on VTK 9.5 and gmsh 4.13.

``LEGOLAS.Locate``: which cell holds a point, and where inside it.
doc.description:
* :meth:`Locate.points` -- the honest search: candidate cells by their
  centroids (k-d tree) and bounding boxes, then Newton on the curved map of
  each hexahedron (Lagrange through its equispaced geometric nodes, any
  order) or barycentric coordinates in a tetrahedron. Reference coordinates
  come back in ``[-1, 1]^3``.
* :meth:`Locate.horses3d_ad` -- what HORSES3D's actuator disk does instead
  (``FindActuatorPointElementAD`` in ``ActuatorDisk.f90``): each MPI rank
  takes the **first** of its elements whose *trilinear* shape (8 corners)
  holds the point, and only that one is tested with the curved shape. A
  point between the chord and the arc of a curved face is then lost, and
  the solver stops with "Actuator disk point not found in mesh". This
  generalises ``check_ad_points.py`` (which only knew Ngeo = 2).
* :func:`read_actuator_points` -- the stations of an
  ``ActuatorDef/Act_ActuatorDiskDef.dat`` (models A and B), as HORSES3D
  places them: plane ``x = x_hub``, angle from +y towards +z.

Prisms and pyramids are not located (their cells are skipped); a point that
only they could hold comes back as outside.

line 7, radius on 11, hub radius on 13, ``n_radial n_azimuthal`` on 15,
then the model block (``# MODEL A`` lists ``r delta_p0 swirl`` from line
20; model B lists ``r chord twist n_polars`` from line 25, each followed
by its polar files).

doc.summary: Reference coordinates of points *x* ``(m, 3)`` in hexahedra with canonical nodes *X* ``(m, n^3, 3)``; returns ``(xi (m, 3), residual)``.
Reference coordinates in the trilinear cells of VTK corners *C*.
``LEGOLAS.Solution``: a HORSES3D solution on the mesh, node by node.
doc.description:
A ``.hsol`` stores, per element, the solution at ``(p+1)**3`` Gauss or
Gauss-Lobatto nodes, in the element order of the mesh ``.h5`` and with ``i``
running fastest along xi. The mesh in LEGOLAS has its own nodes: the
geometric ones, equispaced, of order Ngeo. :meth:`Solution.load` evaluates
the solution's polynomial of each element at those nodes, so the viewer can
colour every face vertex with the value of *its* element: the jumps of a DG
solution between elements stay visible, nothing is averaged.

Checked on 24/11/2026 against the solver itself: the LEGOLAS geometry
evaluated at the solution nodes reproduces the coordinates of HORSES3D's
``.hmesh`` to 1e-14 (turbine, Gauss nodes, p = 2, 3, 4; sphere,
Gauss-Lobatto, p = 2). Element order, node order and node positions are
therefore the solver's.

Variables: with the 5 conservative variables, ``rho``, ``u``, ``v``, ``w``,
``p``, ``T``, ``Mach``, ``Cp`` (:func:`FotR.solver_tools.horses3d.
primitive_variables`; incompressible runs have no ``T`` nor ``Mach``) and
``Vmag``. They are computed at the solution nodes and then interpolated.
Other files keep their raw components ``q0``, ``q1``…

Not yet: statistics files (``.stats.hsol``, which the reader core does not
decode), p-adaptive solutions, gradients (vorticity, Q criterion) and
surfaces (``.surf.hsol``).

doc.summary: HOPR / PyHOPE ``*_mesh.h5`` meshes (the input mesh of HORSES3D and FLEXI).
doc.description:
Layout (checked against PyHOPE 0.11 files on 20/11/2026):

* ``NodeCoords`` repeats every node once per element that uses it;
  ``GlobalNodeIDs`` (1-based) says which unique node each row is.
* ``ElemInfo`` rows: ``[type, zone, first side, last side, first node,
  last node]``, ranges half-open and 0-based. Types: ``104/204`` tetra,
  ``105/115/205`` pyramid, ``106/116/206`` prism, ``108/118/208`` hexa
  (``1xx`` straight, ``2xx`` curved).
* Hexahedron nodes are in tensor order, ``i`` fastest, **also for the linear
  108/118** — LEGOLAS's canonical layout, no permutation needed. Verified by
  matching every element face with its neighbour's (100 % on the sphere
  g1/g2 and the wind-turbine g4 meshes).
* ``SideInfo`` rows: ``[side type, global side, neighbour elem (1-based,
  0 none), 10*neighbour local side + flip, BC id (1-based, 0 none)]``.
  The sides of an element come in CGNS face order.
* ``BCNames`` / ``BCType`` (``[type, curved, state, alpha]``); type 100 is
  an inner zone (it marks faces with an element on each side). Such a face
  carries the BC id on **both** of its sides; LEGOLAS keeps it once, on the
  element with the lower index.

doc.summary: CGNS meshes, read with h5py (CGNS/HDF5 only; no CGNS library needed).
doc.description:
A CGNS/HDF5 file is an HDF5 tree where every CGNS node is a group with
attributes ``label`` and ``name`` and, if it carries data, a dataset called
``" data"`` (leading space). Strings are stored as int8 arrays.

Supported: unstructured zones, element sections of any fixed type or
``MIXED`` (with or without ``ElementStartOffset``), and boundaries given
by ``ZoneBC/BC_t`` (``PointList``/``PointRange`` on faces or on vertices).
Without ``ZoneBC``, each surface section becomes a boundary named after
it, which is what ANSA writes. Not supported: structured zones,
``NGON_n``/``NFACE_n`` polyhedra, CGNS/ADF files.

Hexahedra in tensor-product types (HEXA_8/27/64/125) are permuted to the
canonical layout; serendipity hexahedra (HEXA_20/32/56/44/98) and
high-order tetrahedra, pyramids and prisms keep their corners only, with a
warning.

returns.desc: Zones of the file become volume zones; with several zones their nodes are not merged (a warning says so), so the interfaces between zones show up as exterior faces.

doc.summary: Append *block*, joining it to an existing one of the same kind/order.
Gmsh ``.msh`` meshes: v2.2 with an own parser, v4 through meshio.
doc.description:
Why an own parser for v2.2: ANSA writes binary v2.2 files in **big-endian**
byte order. The format allows it (the integer ``1`` after the header tells
the byte order, and gmsh honours it), but meshio assumes little-endian and
fails with a bare "Couldn't read file". The v2.2 parser below reads ASCII
and binary files in either byte order; v4 files go to meshio.

Physical groups give the names: dimension-3 groups become volume zones and
dimension-2 groups become boundaries (a physical surface declared without
elements becomes an empty boundary). Surfaces without a physical group are
grouped by their geometrical entity (``entity_<tag>``).

Node orders: the v2.2 parser keeps gmsh's native order
(:data:`..ordering.GMSH_HEX`); meshio hands back ``hexahedron27`` in VTK
order but ``hexahedron64``/``hexahedron125`` in gmsh's
(:data:`..ordering.MESHIO_HEX`). Serendipity hexahedra and high-order
tetrahedra, pyramids and prisms keep their corners only, with a warning.

Files exported by ANSA at order 4 have been seen with a node ordering of
their own (neither gmsh nor CGNS); the tensor-order screen in
:func:`..io.read` then warns.

doc.summary: HORSES3D ``.hmesh`` files: the solution nodes the solver actually used.
doc.description:
The file stores, per element, the ``(N+1)**3`` solution nodes in tensor
order and nothing else: no connectivity, no boundary names. LEGOLAS rebuilds
the connectivity by merging coincident nodes, which only works for
Gauss-Lobatto nodes (they sit on the element faces); with Gauss nodes the
elements share nothing, so every face counts as exterior and a warning says
so. The order here is the polynomial order ``p`` of the solution, not the
geometric order of the mesh. Reading goes through
:func:`FotR.solver_tools.horses3d.read_mesh`.

params.desc: Merge tolerance relative to the bounding-box diagonal.

returns.desc: One hexahedral block of order ``p``; no boundaries.
